items.title: What I learned at Verde
items.contentHtml:
This is the third time I am writing this. The other two went wrong. Fuck the BS, let's get into what matters, learnings in hf stuff, AI and life.

Hedge Fund Stuff

1. Excel without mouse - makes life easier and more colorful. No friction. Just direct work2. How markets rlly work - this is hard to define exactly, but before Verde, Faria Lima/Wall Street was a idealist company. "sell-side", "earnings preview", "expectations" were all kind of idealist terms that reflect much more stronger views than actually are. I talked with sell-side. I did my earnings preview. They fucking bought the stock. They are just people, smart (sometimes) people doing their job, hoping to get promoted, get rich and spend with their families or at Vila JK at night. Sell-side reports are not sacred art works which represent the maximum level of enterprise intelligence society has achieved. They are just some junior analyst writing numbers that the senior analyst said while the partner was thinking if this was going to hurt company reputation. Every time you think they are some kind of fucking genius, remember that story about the education company who released 4 semesters instead of 3 in their earnings. They released saying it was a error. The stock grew by two-figures in the next day (just to make it clear THEY SAID IT WAS A FUCKING ERROR). Not just that, in the next year, the analysts FUCKING forgot that the number in the model in the previous year was wrong and, using that as parameters, grew their numbers by roughly 33% of what it should be. Like, what'd fuck.3. How to think about stocks - there are three components to return: earnings increase, multiple re-rating, dividends. It all boils down to those three. That's what matter.4. DDM > DCF - kind of contrarian here, but it's a rlly interesting approach. in the end is the money that you are receiving through dividends that matters. They should be close to each other (mainly DDM to FCFE) but they are not. Interesting take5. Modelling stuff - not just excel. But like. How to properly do a fuckin 3sm. 6. Building a portfolio - x-axis assimetry. y-axis conviction. markovitz in action. Simple, visual, but insightful about what matters. 7. Hypothesis - How a thesis should look like. Testable, measurable, specific. Exactly like a popper scientific hypothesis (wooow). That is cool. Making a scientific approach is exactly the type of intelectual shit I like about markets. Not BS, but a real philosophy to make work better.

AI

1. Explicit x Implicit - That is the one I want to dive and learn the most. The problem with AI use is that we don't a know a bunch of shit we know. That's what they call "judgement" or "taste". These are the things we can make and we know. But we cannot teach. Because it is implicit. I have to read more and learn here, but for me this seems to be part of the bottleneck of becoming an AI powered human being. (the other part is knowing what you want. and that's even harder, but more later)2. When you know what you want, you're set - my boss only wanted a dashboard where he could see the information that mattered, and some skill that did the modelling for him. simple. sweet. my only job was to ask claude to make it, and ask again when said it didn't. like, you just need to ask and don't be a retarded. Just agency (or whatever that word is supposed to mean)3. It's about the mindset - what can I simplify in my life. Do i know what I want? 

Life

x. The processx. What is the best frameworkx. Divergence x Convergencex. psychopaths win

items.title: Removing Friction
items.contentHtml:
I wanna do X. I am in Y. What are the things that do not matter and that make this transition harder?

That is friction. 
  • Want to learn about x? Have to spend time going across tabs, twitter, spotify, etc. Friction.
  • Want to recruit for IB? Have to spend time keeping track of emails, answers, etc. Friction.
Removing friction is important because of two main factors. Firstly, it takes time. No one wants do spend time on shit that no one gives a fuck. Secondly, and I think the most important one: it reduces the enthusiasm and willingness to do what really matters. Living 2min from the gym? Amazing. No lazy excuses. Have to take 3 buses, 2 trains, and walk 3 miles. No fucking way. What are the "frictions" of my life? Can AI solve any of them?
  • Learning -> Solved
  • Recruiting and keeping track of all the BS -> In process
  • What else there is? Beyond removing shit that does not matter, how can it empower the ones that do?
